title: A broken compass
literal_translation: My compass is broken.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I have lost the direction of a plan.
usage_context: A plan has become confusing after unexpected news.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not every broken navigation tool signifies an existential crisis.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The closed page
literal_translation: I close a book.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am ending this discussion for now.
usage_context: A debate has become exhausting or repetitive.
counterexample_and_restriction: It does not mean the underlying facts have disappeared.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A wing at the door
literal_translation: I stay at the doorway.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am staying close without intruding.
usage_context: Someone is waiting nearby while a friend needs space.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a replacement for asking permission to enter.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Tomorrow's unfilled page
qaroshi: zher mi yurayaro shima-m nu shiroli.
literal_translation: I do not write tomorrow's book.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I refuse to pretend to know the future.
usage_context: Someone wants a confident prediction without evidence.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a refusal to make any plans at all.
sound_out: zhehr mee yoo-rah-YAH-roh SHEE-mahm noo shee-ROH-lee.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The star behind the window
literal_translation: I see a star through the window.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I have a distant but real possibility in sight.
usage_context: A person is considering a faraway goal.
counterexample_and_restriction: It does not assert the goal will be reached.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Two visible doors
literal_translation: I see doors.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I see two possible paths but lack a criterion.
usage_context: A decision has several options with tradeoffs.
counterexample_and_restriction: Seeing actual doors is normally literal.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The feather that stayed
literal_translation: I guard a feather at home.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I cherish a small reminder of someone.
usage_context: A modest object carries a personal memory.
counterexample_and_restriction: Does not establish the original owner or story.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Rain over a promise
literal_translation: I protect a promise in the rain.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I remain committed when conditions worsen.
usage_context: A public commitment becomes difficult.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not evidence that fulfilling it is actually safe or possible.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A river with no answer
literal_translation: I ask a river.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I seek an answer where none can be given.
usage_context: An anxious person repeats the wrong kind of question.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not an insult toward someone who is silent.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The library after dusk
literal_translation: I read a book at night.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I work patiently without public attention.
usage_context: Quiet study or unrecognized effort.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not proof of knowledge merely because a book was read.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A fire behind glass
literal_translation: I watch fire through a window.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I feel emotion strongly but keep distance from it.
usage_context: Someone is observing a conflict instead of joining it.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not every physical fire symbolizes conflict.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A promise with a date
literal_translation: I write a promise for today.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I limit a commitment to what I can responsibly promise.
usage_context: Someone rejects an impossible eternal vow.
counterexample_and_restriction: A dated promise still requires actual follow-through.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The borrowed wing
literal_translation: I fly with a friend.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I accept practical help rather than pretending independence.
usage_context: A learner receives support for a hard task.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a claim that companionship removes all risk.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A mouth full of stars
literal_translation: I speak stars.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am speaking with exaggerated enthusiasm.
usage_context: Excited celebration of an ambitious idea.
counterexample_and_restriction: Can sound absurd in serious or technical reporting.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: An empty map
literal_translation: I have no compass.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I cannot identify a reliable route yet.
usage_context: Uncertainty about how to proceed.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a literal assertion that no physical instrument exists.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The house that listened
literal_translation: The home listens to me.
proposed_figurative_meaning: This place feels emotionally safe.
usage_context: A cherished roost or remembered family refuge.
counterexample_and_restriction: Buildings are not literally capable of hearing speech.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A question in the nest
literal_translation: I guard a question at home.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am not ready to discuss a private uncertainty.
usage_context: A sensitive issue needs reflection.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a reason to suppress another person's rights.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Writing on water
literal_translation: I write a memory on water.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I attempt to preserve something fleeting.
usage_context: Fragile memories or a temporary idea.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not reliable archival advice or a literal storage medium.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The shadow of the wing
literal_translation: I see a wing at night.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I notice traces of a departed companion.
usage_context: Grief triggered by an everyday reminder.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not automatically evidence of supernatural presence.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The quiet bridge
literal_translation: I remain at the bridge.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am pausing at the point between two choices.
usage_context: An unresolved transition or decision.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not every delay counts as courage.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A feather against the storm
literal_translation: I protect a feather during a storm.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I safeguard something small under heavy pressure.
usage_context: Care for a fragile relationship or work.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a safety recommendation to risk injury for an object.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The door that asks first
literal_translation: Am I permitted to stay in the home?
proposed_figurative_meaning: I will not assume welcome or consent.
usage_context: Entering a personal or social space.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not all door questions are idioms.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A map with another name
literal_translation: I ask the compass.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am leaning too heavily on one tool's answer.
usage_context: Someone refuses to check conflicting evidence.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a claim that instruments have feelings.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A song without an audience
literal_translation: I speak a song.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I create without expecting approval.
usage_context: Private practice, personal creative expression.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a dismissal of public performers.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The last page remains blank
literal_translation: I do not write in the book.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I leave the outcome unresolved rather than invent facts.
usage_context: Reporting an unknown ending.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not evidence of authorial laziness without context.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The flight that waited
qaroshi: nëm mi goro-yu, ro mi nëru-te.
literal_translation: I will fly, because I rested.
proposed_figurative_meaning: Preparing patiently can make future action possible.
usage_context: A flyer remembers the value of rest before a long journey.
counterexample_and_restriction: Rest does not substitute for permission, preparation or a weather report.
sound_out: nuhm mee goh-ROH-yoo, roh mee nuh-ROO-teh.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A friend in the margins
literal_translation: I write a friend into the book.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I give someone quiet credit in a story.
usage_context: Acknowledging overlooked help.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not permission to publish private information.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Toward the river
literal_translation: I will travel to the river.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am ready to consider life beyond the present challenge.
usage_context: A new phase after hard work.
counterexample_and_restriction: No guarantee that a journey itself solves problems.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The untouched key
literal_translation: I do not look at the compass.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I choose to listen rather than overplan.
usage_context: A conversation requires attention, not navigation.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not good advice to ignore navigational safety.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Three steps before the jump
qaroshi: dal mi goro-ki, ro mi wëmi-te.
literal_translation: I can fly, because I worked.
proposed_figurative_meaning: Preparation has made a difficult task possible.
usage_context: A learner earns competence through practice.
counterexample_and_restriction: Ability still does not equal permission.
sound_out: dahl mee goh-ROH-kee, roh mee wuh-MEE-teh.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The honest future
literal_translation: I do not know the future.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I can be honest without predicting outcomes.
usage_context: Someone is pressured to give certainty.
counterexample_and_restriction: No claim about physical clocks or time travel.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The softest refusal
literal_translation: I will not fly, tenderly.
proposed_figurative_meaning: A boundary can be firm without being cruel.
usage_context: Declining a cherished invitation.
counterexample_and_restriction: A tender resonance does not cancel the refusal.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The open hand at the market
literal_translation: I give you a book with gratitude.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I choose generosity over bargaining.
usage_context: A trade becomes a gift.
counterexample_and_restriction: A gift must not be interpreted as a requirement to reciprocate.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: Guarding a grieving story
literal_translation: I protect a story with sorrow.
proposed_figurative_meaning: A memory deserves careful stewardship.
usage_context: A narrative about grief or an absent friend.
counterexample_and_restriction: A story can still be false; emotional weight is not evidence.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The mountain in the mirror
literal_translation: I see a mountain.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I recognize a difficulty I had avoided.
usage_context: Facing a personal challenge.
counterexample_and_restriction: A mountain sighting is normally literal.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: An answer still in flight
literal_translation: Will I answer the question?
proposed_figurative_meaning: I am willing to consider an answer but not ready yet.
usage_context: A difficult conversation is in progress.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not an affirmative answer to the underlying question.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The sky is not a signature
literal_translation: I do not write the sky.
proposed_figurative_meaning: A grand declaration is not a concrete promise.
usage_context: Someone offers inspiring words without actionable commitment.
counterexample_and_restriction: Not a claim that the sky can literally sign documents.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The wing that stayed home
literal_translation: My wing stays at home.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I choose rest over performative bravery.
usage_context: A flyer postpones travel for health or safety.
counterexample_and_restriction: Does not deny the speaker's ability to fly.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: A letter in two hands
literal_translation: I write a message with you.
proposed_figurative_meaning: We are jointly responsible for a difficult conversation.
usage_context: Friends compose a response together.
counterexample_and_restriction: Joint writing does not guarantee equal understanding.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested

title: The first honest silence
literal_translation: I do not speak.
proposed_figurative_meaning: I acknowledge that I lack a warranted answer.
usage_context: An investigation before evidence arrives.
counterexample_and_restriction: Silence can also have unrelated motivations.
status: individually written editorial metaphor proposal, not conventionalized/attested
